articles.title: Wind threatens 100th Macy's parade balloons as snow aims at St. Louis
articles.summary: Over 44 million people were under alerts Wednesday, with gusts up to 70 mph possible from South Carolina to Massachusetts. Illinois and Missouri face up to 6 inches of snow, 9 in spots. In New York, balloons are grounded if winds reach 23 mph sustained or gust to 34 mph.

articles.title: King tides push San Francisco water to a record November high
articles.summary: The Crissy Field tide gauge hit 8.23 feet Tuesday morning, topping the November mark of 7.97 feet set in 1982, the National Weather Service said. Wednesday's high tide could reach 8.5 feet, so more records may fall.

articles.title: Thanksgiving travel: Northeast airports brace for big delays as storms hit both coasts
articles.summary: Rain spreads across the Southeast on Wednesday, then heavy rain and strong gusts reach the mid-Atlantic and Northeast on Thanksgiving Day, when significant delays are expected at all of the region's hub airports. The Pacific Northwest stays wet with mountain snow, and Saturday looks like a decent travel day for most.

articles.title: King tides and Pacific storms could bring historic flooding to the Bay Area
articles.summary: Full-moon king tides plus onshore winds and waves could push West Coast water levels toward record territory, peaking Wednesday. Around San Francisco Bay, water could rise 3 feet above normally dry ground, putting parts of SFO at risk. Coastal Flood Warnings run through Thursday.

articles.title: Fast-moving East Coast storm to bring wind, rain and flooding on Thanksgiving
articles.summary: A coastal storm will push up the East Coast from Wednesday into Friday, with peak impacts in much of the Northeast on Thanksgiving Day. Many areas could see 1 to 4 inches of rain and gusts over 50 mph, while king tides could worsen coastal flooding, especially around Charleston, South Carolina.

articles.title: Thanksgiving storm could turn rain to wet snow in parts of the Midwest
articles.summary: A storm arriving late Wednesday may pull in enough cold air to change rain to wet snow or a wintry mix in parts of Illinois, Indiana, Ohio and Michigan, most likely Thursday afternoon and night. Highways like I-70, I-75 and I-94 and airports in Chicago, Detroit and Cleveland could see delays.

articles.title: Earth logs its most abnormally hot day on record
articles.summary: Preliminary Copernicus data show the globe ran 2.12°C above the preindustrial average on Nov. 20. Scientists point to human-caused warming plus a powerful, still-growing El Niño, and say more days above 2°C are likely in the coming months.

articles.title: Storm after storm to bring rain and feet of mountain snow to the West this week
articles.summary: A string of storms starts Tuesday with rain from Washington into Northern California, adding to flooding in already soaked areas. The Sierra Nevada, Cascades and Rockies could get feet of snow, and coastal flood alerts cover the Bay Area and Southern California. Flight delays are expected at Seattle-Tacoma and San Francisco airports.

articles.title: A century of Macy's parade weather, from snow to balloon-grounding wind
articles.summary: With the 100th Macy's parade days away, The Weather Channel looked back at its weather extremes: 1971 was the only year every balloon stayed grounded, 1989 brought 4.4 inches of snow, and 2018 was the coldest at 17 degrees. Strong gusts in 1997 led to the city's balloon wind limits. This year's outlook hints at a cold, wet morning.
